  :63:19 - error TS2554: Expected 2 arguments, but got 1.
  :74:13 - error TS2322: Type 'string' is not assignable to type 'ReactElement<any, string | JSXElementConstructor<any>>'.

Cause of :63 — the component calls `t('entityRenamedNotice.dismiss')` but NO such key exists in plugins/catalog-react/src/translation.ts. That file declares only `entityRenamedNotice.title` and `entityRenamedNotice.description` (see the context file, around line 188). Cause of :74 — the `BuiAlert` (@backstage/ui Alert) `description` prop expects a ReactElement, not a plain string, so passing the `description` string directly fails.

Fix BOTH, minimally:
  - For :63, add a `dismiss` entry to the `entityRenamedNotice` block in plugins/catalog-react/src/translation.ts (a short adopter-facing label such as 'Dismiss'), keeping that file's exact existing style and indentation, and keep the `t('entityRenamedNotice.dismiss')` call. Do NOT hard-code an English string in the component.
  - For :74, wrap the description in the element the prop expects (for example a fragment or span) so it typechecks, without changing the visible text.

Change nothing else. Keep the component's behaviour, both UI vocabularies (legacy @material-ui/lab Alert and the bui branch), the dismiss-on-click behaviour, the location.state reading, and the Apache 2.0 header. Its own test must keep passing, and the file must typecheck.

Answer with the component file as your artifact; the translation.ts change is listed as a context file and you must state the exact edit needed to it in your answer if you cannot write it — but prefer writing the component so that it uses a key you also add.       lookupResult?.ref === requestedRef ? lookupResult.entity : undefined;
